correctness.rationale: I reconstructed the phase matrix using polynomial spectral projectors of the six-cycle adjacency matrix, rather than evaluating the bundled formulas alone. The two proposed cosines satisfy c²=(1−sqrt(6)/2)c+sqrt(6)/4, and their weighted mean is (1−sqrt(6))/10. This gives the moments through degree four by the two-term recurrence; exact substitution into the four distance classes gives 1/6 in every case. The cosines are distinct and in (−1,1) (e.g. sqrt(6)<2.5, sqrt(10)<3.2 and sqrt(6)>2.2); the weight perturbation has magnitude less than 1/2. Equality of the distance-one and distance-two probabilities forces c=0,1,−1/2, giving distance-one probabilities 1/9,0,0. Translation and reflection cover all entries. Integral eigenvalues give a common 2π shift, so both times can be put strictly beyond any cutoff.
residual_risks: Only the specified unweighted adjacency evolution and exact expected matrix are certified; no claim about all two-time laws or robustness.
